content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable AI workflows that are easy to invoke and review. This skill helps create, update, validate, and document Claude Code slash commands.
actual_capabilities: Explains command file locations for project, user, and plugin scopes.
Defines required and optional frontmatter fields for Claude Code commands.
Provides templates for arguments, workflows, examples, and error handling.
Guides model field choices with version aliases and full model IDs.
Includes a Python validator for naming, YAML, tools, models, arguments, and examples.
Supplies security checklists for Bash usage, path handling, secrets, and tool permissions.
limitations: It focuses on Claude Code slash command files, not general plugin development.
The validator checks structure and common patterns, not full runtime safety.
Model examples may need review against current provider documentation.
Commands that use Bash still require human review before use.

use_cases.title: Create Team Commands
use_cases.description: Build reusable slash commands for testing, reviewing, scaffolding, and documentation workflows.

use_cases.title: Standardize Existing Commands
use_cases.description: Review command files for schema quality, naming rules, model format, examples, and tool permissions.

use_cases.title: Design Safer Automation
use_cases.description: Plan command workflows with argument validation, least-privilege tools, and clear safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code slash command for [task]. Ask for the command name, arguments, tools, and expected output before writing it.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my slash command at [path]. Check frontmatter, argument documentation, tool permissions, model format, examples, and security notes.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Model Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Update commands in [directory] so model fields use version aliases or full model IDs. Report each change and validation result.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Command Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a namespaced set of slash commands for [workflow]. Include names, arguments, least-privilege tools, validation rules, and testing steps.

output_examples.input: Create a command to run unit tests for a selected package.
output: A proposed command name and file location.
Recommended argument structure for the package path.
Minimal tool permissions for reading files and running tests.
Workflow steps, examples, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Review an existing command that uses Bash and file arguments.
output: A checklist of frontmatter, naming, and argument documentation issues.
Security notes for path validation and shell argument handling.
Suggested edits that reduce tool permissions where possible.

output_examples.input: Fix commands that use short model aliases.
output_examples.output: A migration summary with affected commands, recommended model values, and validation follow-up.

best_practices: Use the smallest tool set that supports the command workflow.
Document every argument with expected format, defaults, and examples.
Validate paths and shell arguments before allowing Bash-based commands.
anti_patterns: Do not create commands with broad tools when read-only access is enough.
Do not pass user arguments directly into shell commands without validation.
Do not use short model aliases in command frontmatter.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create and update Claude Code slash commands stored as Markdown files with YAML frontmatter.

faq.question: Can it validate an existing command?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance and a validator script for common schema, naming, model, and documentation checks.

faq.question: Does it run the commands it creates?
faq.answer: No. It provides command files and validation guidance. Execution depends on user approval and tool settings.

faq.question: Why does it discuss model aliases?
faq.answer: Claude Code commands need version aliases or full model IDs. Short aliases can cause command execution errors.

faq.question: Is Bash required for every command?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends Bash only when needed and encourages least-privilege tool permissions.

faq.question: Can Codex users learn from it?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex users can use the patterns to design AI command workflows, but the file format targets Claude Code.
